During adolescence the body clock shifts by roughly two hours, so a student ordered to be in class at eight is being asked to wake in the middle of their biological {{b1}}. Schools that moved the first lesson later reported fewer absences and a modest {{b2}} in test scores, and, to the surprise of many parents, no loss of time for sport. The change costs almost nothing beyond redrawing the bus {{b3}}, and yet most districts still {{b4}} to make it.

payload.text: Most of the plastic in the sea is not floating in one great island of rubbish. Sunlight and waves break it into fragments so small that they slip through any {{b1}} a ship can tow, and the pieces then sink or are swallowed. Cleaning the open ocean is therefore far less {{b2}} than stopping the plastic at the dozen or so rivers that deliver most of it. That work is unglamorous, and it takes place where the people who fund such {{b3}} rarely go, which may explain why the floating machines attract so much of the {{b4}}.

gaps.before: The photographs taken that evening cast serious
gaps.after: on the account the witness had given to the police.
options: doubt
question
suspicion
disbelief
gaps.explanation: cast doubt on ~（～に疑いを投げかける）は決まった組み合わせ。question は call ~ into question の形で使い、cast question on とは言わない。suspicion は cast suspicion on ~ で「人に嫌疑をかける」意味になり、供述の信頼性には合わない。disbelief は「信じられない気持ち」で cast とは組まない。

gaps.before: The minister insisted that every application
gaps.after: by an independent panel before any money was released.
options: be reviewed
is reviewed
was reviewed
will be reviewed
gaps.explanation: insist that ... のように「要求・提案」を表す動詞の後の that 節では、動詞は原形（仮定法現在）になるので be reviewed が正しい。is / was / will be reviewed はいずれも時制のある形で、この構文では使えない。

gaps.before: The first two trials produced almost identical results.
gaps.after: , the third found no effect at all.
options: By contrast
As a result
In short
Likewise
gaps.explanation: 「最初の2回はほぼ同じ結果」→「3回目は効果なし」という対比なので By contrast が合う。As a result は因果、In short は要約、Likewise は「同様に」で前後が同じ内容のときに使うため、いずれも対比をつなげない。

building

payload.title: The Ships That Learned to Slow Down
paragraphs: A container ship burns fuel roughly in proportion to the cube of its speed. Cut the speed by a tenth and the fuel bill falls by nearly a third, which is why, during the trade slump that followed 2008, owners quietly told their captains to throttle back. The practice acquired a name, slow steaming, and it was adopted for the plainest of reasons: with freight rates on the floor, fuel was the one large cost a company could still control.

The environmental effect was an accident, and a large one. Shipping moves about ninety per cent of world trade and releases roughly as much carbon dioxide each year as Germany, so a fleet-wide cut in fuel use is not a small saving. Slower ships are quieter too, and the noise of propellers is now known to disturb the way whales feed and find one another. None of this was the industry’s aim; it was simply what happened when the accountants won an argument.

Making the habit permanent is harder than it sounds. A slower fleet needs more ships to carry the same cargo, and building them releases carbon of its own. Perishable cargo, and factories that run on parts arriving exactly when they are wanted, will pay for speed whatever the fuel costs. Regulators have therefore begun to write speed into the rules rather than leave it to the freight market, on the reasonable assumption that when rates rise again, captains will be told to open the throttle.

questions.prompt: 本文の主旨として最も適切なものはどれですか。
options: Ships slowed down in order to save money, the environmental benefits that followed were unintended, and regulators now want speed written into the rules rather than left to the market.
Shipping companies reduced their speed mainly in order to protect whales from the noise made by their propellers.
Slow steaming has already removed most of the carbon emissions of shipping, so no further regulation of the industry is needed.
Because a slower fleet needs more ships, slow steaming raises emissions overall and the practice should be abandoned.

questions.before: Owners first told their captains to slow down because
questions.after: at a time when freight rates left them almost no other saving to make.
options: fuel was the largest cost still under their control
new rules on underwater noise had just come into force
there were not enough ships available to carry the cargo
engineers had shown that slower engines last much longer

questions.prompt: 速度を落としたことによる環境面の利点が、業界のねらいではなかったことを最もよく示している語句はどれですか。

spans.text: burns fuel roughly in proportion to the cube of its speed
it was simply what happened when the accountants won an argument
building them releases carbon of its own

questions.sentence: In other words, the cleanest thing the industry has ever done was chosen for reasons that had nothing to do with the climate.

questions.prompt: 筆者が本文全体で最も伝えたいことはどれですか。
options: Slow steaming shows that a decision taken purely to cut costs can bring real environmental gains, but because those gains rest on the price of fuel rather than on any intention, they have to be secured by rules.
Since shipping carries ninety per cent of world trade, any attempt to limit the speed of ships would damage the world economy and ought to be resisted.
The strongest argument for slow steaming is the protection of whales, and the saving of fuel is only a minor side benefit.
Speed limits are unnecessary, because shipping companies have shown that they will keep their ships slow without being told to.

payload.title: The Four-Day Week, Measured
paragraphs: The idea sounds like a gift and is usually sold as one: five days of pay for four days of work. What made the recent trials worth reading was that they were not run as favours. Firms joining the largest of them agreed in advance to a rule known as one hundred, eighty, one hundred: full pay, four-fifths of the time, and the same output as before. Almost every company that finished the trial chose to keep the arrangement.

The gains did not come from working faster. Teams cut the things that had survived only because nobody had ever counted their cost: meetings that could have been a message, reports that no one read, the habit of copying a dozen colleagues into every email. Where output held up, it held up because a week of work had been examined honestly for the first time in years. Where it fell, the reason was almost always that the job was tied to somebody else’s clock: a shop that must open, a ward that must be staffed, a customer who calls on Friday.

That distinction matters for what the trials can prove. The firms that volunteer are mostly small, mostly office-based, and led by people who already believed the idea would work; a hospital cannot cut its meetings and send a fifth of its staff home. Sceptics add that part of the reported gain is the ordinary enthusiasm of doing something new, which fades. The honest conclusion is narrower than the headlines, but it is not nothing: for a certain kind of work, a great deal of the week turns out to be waste, and a shorter deadline is what exposes it.

questions.prompt: 本文の主旨として最も適切なものはどれですか。
options: The trials worked mainly by forcing firms to cut low-value work, but the result fits a limited kind of job and cannot simply be extended to every workplace.
The trials show that employees can produce the same output in four days provided they work faster and take fewer breaks.
Because the firms in the trials were small and enthusiastic, the results mean nothing and no company should change its hours.
The main obstacle to a four-day week is the cost of paying five days of wages, which most firms cannot afford.

options: the work had to match somebody else’s timetable
employees were paid for four days rather than five
managers had cancelled too many of their meetings
the trial had run for less than a full year

questions.prompt: この試験の結果をそのまま一般化できない理由を最もよく示している語句はどれですか。

spans.text: full pay, four-fifths of the time, and the same output as before
meetings that could have been a message
The firms that volunteer are mostly small, mostly office-based
a shorter deadline is what exposes it

questions.sentence: The saving, in other words, came out of the week itself rather than out of the people working it.

questions.prompt: 筆者が本文全体で最も伝えたいことはどれですか。
options: The trials suggest that much of a typical office week is low-value activity which a shorter deadline strips out, though the finding holds for a limited range of jobs and may partly reflect the novelty of the change.
The trials prove that every organisation, hospitals and shops included, could move to four days without any loss of output.
Because enthusiasm for anything new always fades, the four-day week produced no real gains at all.
The chief lesson of the trials is that workers value extra pay more highly than extra free time.
